This page corresponds to the exact occupation U.S. O*NET/SOC 49-9099.01 'Geothermal Technicians': perform technical activities at power plants or individual installations necessary for the generation of power from geothermal energy sources, monitor and control operating activities at geothermal power generation facilities and perform maintenance and repairs as necessary, and install, test, and maintain residential and commercial geothermal heat pumps. Official scope text: Perform technical activities at power plants or individual installations necessary for the generation of power from geothermal energy sources. Monitor and control operating activities at geothermal power generation facilities and perform maintenance and repairs as necessary. Install, test, and maintain residential and commercial geothermal heat pumps. Common job titles include Geothermal Service Technician, I and C Technician (instrumentation and control technician), I and E Technician (instrumentation and electrical technician), Operations and Maintenance Technician, Operations Technician, Operator Technician, Plant Electrical Technician, Plant Mechanic, and Plant Technician. The core tasks listed by O*NET include: monitor and adjust the operation of geothermal plant equipment or systems (importance 83); write and maintain work logs, reports, or other documents (83); identify and correct faults in geothermal plant equipment and electrical systems and instrumentation or controls (81); collect and record operating data from the geothermal plant or well field (81); determine whether emergency or auxiliary systems are needed under extreme weather conditions to maintain building heating or cooling (72); perform pre- and post-installation pressure, flow, and related tests on vertical and horizontal geothermal loop piping (69); and identify equipment options such as compressors and make appropriate selections (66). Supplemental tasks include: adjust generation systems to meet load and distribution demand (88); maintain electrical switchgear and process control and transmitters and instrumentation and control equipment according to plant procedures (79); calculate residential heat loss and heat gain coefficients to determine the heating and cooling capacity needed for a ground source heat pump (79); maintain and verify or repair plant instrumentation and control and electronic devices (79); install and maintain plant electrical protection equipment (73); design and lay out geothermal heating systems according to building characteristics and heating and cooling demand and piping and equipment requirements and applicable regulations (73); install and maintain geothermal system instrumentation or controls (72); carry out flushing and venting and other commissioning preparations for newly installed geothermal heating systems (67); weld high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and similar piping (butt fusion, socket fusion, sidewall fusion, and electrofusion) (66); test water source flow and contaminants and other indicators (66); install and maintain or repair ground source or water source coupled heat pumps (66); integrate water heater systems with geothermal heat exchange systems (65); determine the most suitable geothermal loop system type for a property (59); excavate trenches and lay piping to depth (54); apply coatings or operate anti-corrosion systems on geothermal plant equipment or structures (54); backfill trenches to protect piping (53); and operate excavators, backhoes, rock breakers, trench compactors, pavement cutters, grout mixing and pumping equipment, loop reels, and coiled tubing units (52). The wage, employment, and industry figures on this page use the parent occupation 49-9099.00 (Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers, All Other) measure presented by O*NET on that page, and are not the measure for the exact occupation 49-9099.01 itself; the measures and boundaries are described in the sections below.

Editorial exercise H1 | 6 complete fictional inputs and reference solutions are given below; independently use 90 minutes to check water volume and heat, existing pressure drop records, missing permit items, versions, handover deadlines, and the cost subtotal. Read paper records only, and do not operate equipment or perform pressure testing, welding, or energizing. Produce a results table, a problem table, a V1→V2 revision table, and a handover within 200 characters.

Fit signals | The work activity importance for U.S. O*NET 49-9099.01 shows: obtaining information (86), making decisions and solving problems (86), communicating with superiors, peers, or subordinates (83), controlling machines and processes (82), operating vehicles, mechanized devices, or equipment (81), handling and moving objects (79), identifying objects, actions, and events (76), organizing, planning, and prioritizing work (76), performing general physical activities (74), and repairing and maintaining mechanical equipment (74) are the most important activities for this occupation; the work context shows face-to-face or personal and team discussions 96% every day, wearing routine protective or safety equipment 84% every day, exposure to hazardous conditions 90% every day, telephone communication 82% every day, working in an enclosed vehicle or operating enclosed equipment 78% every day, outdoor exposure to all weather 83% every day, and exposure to contaminants 74% every day; work hours 71% more than 40 hours per week; and responsibility for the health and safety of others 63% very high responsibility. If you are willing to work hands-on between plant equipment and building sites, can operate and test according to procedures and judge anomalies from parameters and instruments, and are glad to work outdoors and under hazardous conditions according to safety requirements, the daily demands of this occupation are closer to how you work.

Caution signals | O*NET also shows (49-9099.01, percentage response measure): exposure to hazardous conditions 90% every day; exposure to contaminants 74% every day; wearing routine protective or safety equipment 84% every day; outdoor exposure to all weather 83% every day; working in an enclosed vehicle or operating enclosed equipment 78% every day; responsibility for the health and safety of others 63% very high responsibility; and work hours 71% more than 40 hours per week. This occupation deals with in-service geothermal plant equipment and instrumentation and control and electrical systems, ground source heat pumps and loop piping, and drilling, excavation, welding, and pressure testing work, and a single unconfirmed work permit or energy isolation, unhandled pressure or flow or electrical parameter excursion, unrecorded failed weld or pressure test, or ground disturbance, confined space, or height work not carried out according to permit can cause personal, equipment, and environmental accidents, and may also involve electric power work safety, special equipment and pressure piping, environmental protection, and occupational health management rules. O*NET lists this occupation in Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation), and the entry education requirement is relatively low but the field safety and certificate requirements are not low. If you find it hard to work hands-on outdoors and under hazardous conditions and noise and contaminants over the long term, find it hard to accept serious consequences of error and personal safety responsibility, or are unwilling to take responsibility for the traceability of testing and maintenance and permit records, you should treat these as real costs that need careful weighing.

A single H1 exercise only observes unit conversion, evidence layering, and handover habits; it cannot prove field installation and repair capability, obtaining qualifications, long-term fit, or personal employment outcomes. If you remain interested, then check the target position's real training, hours, and activity requirements.

Comparison task objects | Geothermal Technicians 49-9099.01 covers geothermal power generation equipment maintenance and ground source heat pump installation and testing, and also includes design and layout, load calculation, and selection; the adjacent positions respectively target hydroelectric, biomass, gas processing, generation control, or grid distribution. Tasks may overlap, and a uniform hierarchy or exclusive responsibility cannot be inferred from the occupational name. Independent activity requires checking real training, qualifications, and institutional authorization, and classification itself does not grant statutory inspection or dispatch approval authority.

Core idea of adjacent positions | Most positions in the same group and adjacent positions aim to 'install, operate, or maintain equipment and systems properly within the boundaries of authorization, safety, and permits and keep records', and the differences lie in the object, output, and authorization level: some take geothermal plant equipment and ground source heat pump sites as their object, some take hydraulic or biomass or boiler equipment, some take operating and monitoring according to procedures, and some take high-voltage electrical maintenance or grid dispatch.

Core purpose of this occupation | Taking in-service geothermal plant equipment and instrumentation and control and electrical systems, ground source heat pumps and loop piping, and field work as its object, complete technical work within the boundaries of drawings, procedures, safety, and permits: monitor and adjust operation, identify and correct faults, carry out installation, testing, maintenance, and repair, and collect and record data, so that equipment and system status and testing and maintenance records are traceable and boundaries can be explained.

Main objects and basis of adjacent positions | Geothermal production managers rely on operating procedures and permit and interconnection and personnel safety rules; hydroelectric plant technicians and biomass plant technicians rely on their own units or fuel and boiler processes and procedures; gas plant operators and power plant operators rely on operating and monitoring procedures; power distributors and dispatchers rely on grid dispatch procedures; electrical repairers and stationary engineers rely on high-voltage electrical and boiler and pressure vessel inspection procedures.

Main objects and basis of this occupation | The objects are geothermal plant equipment and instrumentation and control and electrical and protection devices, ground source heat pumps and buried pipe loops and piping, welding and pressure testing and flushing and commissioning processes, and ground disturbance, confined space, and hazardous work permits; the basis is drawings and process cards and manufacturer requirements and pressure piping and special equipment procedures and electric power work safety and occupational health and environmental protection requirements, along with institutional process and quality rules.

Occupational profile | Geothermal power generation equipment, instrumentation and control, electrical and mechanical maintenance, and ground source heat pump and loop installation, testing, and maintenance can all fall under 49-9099.01. Common titles include Geothermal Service Technician, I and C Technician, O&M Technician, and Plant Mechanic. 96% answer face-to-face every day, 90% hazardous conditions every day, 83% outdoors every day, and 71% a typical week over 40 hours, all context response categories rather than every worker's experience or accident probabilities. U.S. industry information comes from the 2024 parent occupation: administrative support 16%, manufacturing 11%, wholesale 11%, construction 10%, and retail 10%, which cannot be treated as a geothermal employer distribution.
This round the 2025 parent occupation industries are administrative support 16%, manufacturing 12%, retail 11%, and wholesale 10%, which are not a geothermal employer distribution, and the older 2024 figures are marked separately.

Core process of adjacent positions | Geothermal production managers focus on operation command and personnel and permit and interconnection management; hydroelectric plant technicians and biomass plant technicians focus on the operation and repair of their own units; gas plant operators and power plant operators focus on operating and monitoring and patrolling according to procedures; power distributors and dispatchers focus on dispatch instructions and distribution actions and records; electrical repairers and stationary engineers focus on the maintenance, testing, and certificate-based work of high-voltage electrical or boiler equipment.

Core process of this occupation | Work preparation and permits, installation or patrol and monitoring and parameter recording, testing and verification and anomaly handling, maintenance, repair, and replacement, records, handover, and review; every step must be documented according to the safety, process, quality, and permit rules and be reviewable by superiors, operations, and quality.

Main outputs of adjacent positions | Geothermal production managers produce operation and maintenance and permit and interconnection management results; hydroelectric plant technicians and biomass plant technicians produce operation and maintenance records for their own units; gas plant operators and power plant operators produce operating actions and parameter records; power distributors and dispatchers produce dispatch and distribution action records; electrical repairers and stationary engineers produce maintenance, testing, and inspection records.

Main outputs of this occupation | Usable installation and commissioning records, patrol and monitoring and parameter records, testing and verification and pressure testing and flushing records, troubleshooting and repair and replacement records, instrumentation and control and electrical and protection device maintenance records, and traceable work permit and permit and training records.

Responsible parties for adjacent positions | Responsibility for positions in the same group and adjacent positions is usually defined by the institution, procedures, and authorization, and the objects of responsibility are mostly on-site safety, equipment, the environment, and supply reliability.

Responsible party for this occupation | This occupation is responsible for the installation, patrol, monitoring, testing, verification, repair, and recording it performs, and for the work and validation carried out according to drawings, process cards, procedures, safety, and permit requirements; matters involving engineering design, statutory inspection of pressure piping and special equipment, interconnection and permit and acceptance conclusions, and major technical renovation schemes are decided according to the rules by positions or institutions with the corresponding qualifications, and this occupation does not replace their decisions.

Authority and approval of adjacent positions | The authority of positions in the same group and adjacent positions comes from institutional authorization, practice or qualification and certificate requirements, procedures, and rules, and usually does not include the authority to decide on its own conclusions, signatures, or data provision beyond its own authorization or scope; matters involving engineering, inspection, permits, compliance, and personal information should be referred to the corresponding position or institution.

Authority and approval of this occupation | Field work, repair, isolation, ground disturbance, confined space, and height work must take place within work permits and permits and the authorized scope; putting instrumentation and protection devices in and out of service and bypassing them require approval according to the procedure; welding, pressure testing, commissioning, and start-up must be carried out according to process cards and procedures and within the authorized scope; matters involving statutory inspection of pressure piping and special equipment, engineering design, interconnection and permit and acceptance conclusions, and environmental protection and occupational health must obtain approval from or be referred to the corresponding position or institution according to the rules, and unauthorized operation or issuing of conclusions is prohibited.

Conclusion boundaries of adjacent positions | Conclusions from positions in the same group and adjacent positions are mostly limited to this project, this process, and this duty level, and usually do not constitute a determination of equipment safety, compliance, or legal liability; cross-disciplinary conclusions and those involving engineering, inspection, permits, or legal use have limits on their applicability.

Conclusion boundaries of this occupation | Work conclusions state only verifiable parameters and testing, verification, repair, and permit records, and distinguish field observation facts from judgment and inference and pending verification; unauthorized judgments and commitments must not be made on matters beyond one's authorization (engineering design, statutory inspection of pressure piping and special equipment, and interconnection and permit and acceptance conclusions); when pressure, flow, or electrical parameters exceed limits, welding or pressure testing fails, instruments are unverified, or records do not match the site, work must be suspended and escalated or referred, and conclusions must also withstand review by superiors, operations, quality, and regulatory inspections.

Pre-entry checking statement | The following six items are used to check item by item before applying and starting the job, to avoid inferring actual duties and authorization from the job title or promotional language; the checking results should be based on written recruitment information, the employment contract, position descriptions, and safety, process, and permit rules and documents, and should be continuously confirmed after starting. This page lists checking directions only and does not constitute a formal conditions list for any institution or project. Special note: this occupation often involves hazardous conditions, contaminants, energized and pressurized equipment, ground disturbance, confined space, and height work, so be sure to confirm the position's specific requirements for safety training, protective equipment, work permits, certificate requirements, and data disclosure.

Notes on checking points | Position titles are similar but duties and authorization differ greatly: some focus on geothermal plant instrumentation and control and electrical maintenance, some on ground source heat pump installation and commissioning, some on loop drilling, excavation, and welding, some on patrol and data recording, and some on repair and testing; different institutions and jurisdictions also differ in the authorization for operating energized and pressurized equipment, welding and pressure testing, ground disturbance and confined space work, and permits and acceptance and data disclosure.

01 Actual duties and authorization boundaries of the position | Check whether the role truly involves independent installation or repair or instrumentation and control maintenance or pressure testing and commissioning work, or is mainly assisting, carrying, and recording; check the tools, instruments, test equipment, vehicles, and data platforms that may be used, the permit, certificate, and protection requirements for energized, pressurized, ground disturbance, confined space, and height work, the approval requirements for external disclosure of records and compliance data, and the collaboration and reporting lines with operations, maintenance, safety, and quality teams.

Notes on checking points | This occupation often involves energized, pressurized, and rotating equipment, ground disturbance, excavation, welding, confined space, and height work, and noise and contaminant conditions, and usually requires electric power work safety and special equipment and occupational health training, protective equipment, work permits, and emergency drill requirements.

02 Safety, environmental, and occupational health requirements | Check whether the institution requires and provides: training and permits for work permits, energy isolation, lockout and tagout, confined space, height work, and ground disturbance work; certificate requirements for the installation, welding, and inspection of pressure piping and special equipment; protection and emergency response requirements for welding, pressure testing, lifting, excavation, and grouting work; requirements for contaminants, waste, excavated soil, noise, and restoration; occupational health, medical examinations, and protection against noise, high temperature, and chemical exposure; equipment inventory and operating data and confidentiality and personal information management requirements; and the reporting and investigation process for accidents, anomalies, and quality problems.

The O*NET catalog lists 5 certification names, which serve only as a discovery entry. On 2026-10-03 IGSHPA was checked: the old AI, CGD, CGI, and CRD courses are being phased out, and AI is arranged case by case only because of related program requirements; the new system is modular by design, installation, service, and inspection directions, and renewals of existing certificates and new registrations are checked separately. AEE CGD has stopped accepting new applications, while existing holders still have a renewal path. NGWA CVCLD is a voluntary closed-loop drilling certification requiring being at least 20 years old, 24 months of continuous related drilling experience, an examination, and documentation, and is not a general zero-experience entry certificate nor a substitute for local licensing. Historical names in the catalog must not be written across the board as currently registrable or required for all geothermal positions.

Pay checking suggestion | Ask about the base wage, bonus types, overtime and shift differentials, benefits, hours, and on-call and travel arrangements; contract items being asked about cannot be described as universal across all positions, and this occupation's income cannot be inferred from parent occupation percentiles.

04 Wages, hours, and employment contract measures | Check the composition of the offered pay (base wage, rotation or shift and site allowances, overtime and maintenance or project performance and bonuses, continuing education and certification support, and protective equipment and tools and vehicle arrangements), the hours, rotation, on-call, maintenance outage, and travel arrangements, the contract term and the unit or project source, the probation period and assessment measures (work quality, safety, records, and collaboration indicators), and whether equipment and process data and trade secrets and intellectual property ownership and insurance arrangements are involved.

Notes on checking points | The interface relationships with operations, maintenance, instrumentation and control, safety, environmental, quality, and contractor parties determine the boundaries of work, records, and responsibility, and must be clarified in advance.

05 Interface authority with operations, maintenance, safety, and quality parties | Check the path for confirming work plans, maintenance windows, outage requests, and isolation requests, the arrangements for using and maintaining instrumentation, test equipment, tools, vehicles, and data platforms, the path for spare parts, materials, vendor support, and deviation handling, the signing of testing and maintenance records and the approval for external submission, the reporting path for anomalies, accidents, environmental, and quality problems, and cross-crew and contractor work and record handover and the division of responsibility.

Notes on checking points | The traceability and recordkeeping requirements for work permits, parameters, testing, verification, repair, training, and permit records determine how safety, quality, and responsibility are defined; the templates, deadlines, revision, archiving, access authority, and retention period specifications must be clarified in advance (data that is controlled, involves trade secrets, or involves personal information must also be managed according to confidentiality and minimum-necessary requirements).

Preface | The comparison below is organized in four columns: 'occupational direction — core work and outputs — key difference — what it is better suited to'. Geothermal, hydroelectric, biomass, natural gas, and electric power operation positions are often linked within the same generation group or energy service provider, but linkage does not mean they are interchangeable; when choosing across directions, the process, procedures, permits, certificates, and responsibility boundaries of that direction must be learned anew.

Key difference | The object is geothermal power generation equipment and ground source heat pumps and loops; the exact tasks also include design and layout, load calculation, and equipment selection. It cannot be inferred that this occupation is uniformly an engineer's assistant or that adjacent occupations have no maintenance or installation duties at all.

Better suited to people who are willing to work hands-on between plant equipment and building sites and trenches, can complete installation, testing, and repair according to drawings, process cards, and procedures, judge anomalies from parameters and instruments and report within authorization, and are willing to work outdoors and under hazardous conditions according to safety and permit requirements.

Core work and outputs: monitor and adjust the operation of geothermal plant equipment or systems, identify and correct equipment and electrical and instrumentation and control faults, maintain and verify instrumentation and control and electronic devices, collect and record operating data and work logs, install, test, and maintain ground source heat pumps and loop piping, carry out pressure testing, flushing, and commissioning preparations, and operate excavation, grouting, and coiled tubing units and similar equipment; outputs are installation, patrol, testing, verification, repair, and record results (O*NET/SOC 49-9099.01).

Responsibility preface | efficiency can be outsourced to tools, but hands-on field work, safety, permits and quality responsibility cannot. The five steps below are the human responsibility points that must be preserved before and after adopting any digital tool.

Requirements and boundaries: work objectives, process requirements, safety boundaries and permit conditions must be determined by personnel with the corresponding authorization; tools do not replace judgment on drawings, processes or work permits.

On-site confirmation and quality: confirming the status of equipment, piping and instruments, and welding, pressure testing, flushing, commissioning, isolation and lockout/tagout must be completed by the individual under procedures and certification requirements; tools do not replace on-site verification or quality determination.

Data and judgment: parameters, test results and analysis trends must be checked and reviewed by the individual; tool output must not be used directly as the basis for energization, commissioning, acceptance or reporting, and judgments must not exceed what procedures and data support.

Safety, permits and data: live, pressurized, excavation, confined space and work-at-height activities, and controlled data or data involving trade secrets or personal information, must be managed under minimum-necessary, permit and retention-period requirements, and tools must not be used to send such data out or to generate unverified content.

Disclosure and change: maintenance plans, permits, acceptance, external disclosure and process changes must stay within the scope of authorization, safety and quality requirements; when parameters exceed limits, pressure tests fail, or records conflict with on-site conditions, report upward per the system.

Occupation definition | The geothermal technicians on this page are the precise occupation O*NET 49-9099.01 (Geothermal Technicians): they perform technical work related to geothermal power generation and geothermal heat pumps at geothermal power plants or single-family and commercial installations, monitor and control the operation of geothermal power facilities and maintain and repair them as needed, and install, test and maintain residential and commercial ground-source heat pumps. Common job titles include Geothermal Service Technician, I and C Technician, I and E Technician, Operations and Maintenance Technician, Plant Mechanic and Plant Technician. The outputs are installation, inspection, testing, calibration, maintenance and record results; the above uses the US measure, while mainland China's systems and statistical measures for electrical safety production, pressure piping, special equipment, environmental protection, occupational health, excavation and confined spaces are described elsewhere on this page.

AEE has stopped accepting new CGD applications, while existing holders still have a renewal path. entries.answer: The geothermal technicians on this page are the precise occupation O*NET 49-9099.01 (Geothermal Technicians): they perform technical work related to geothermal power generation and geothermal heat pumps at geothermal power plants or single-family and commercial installations, monitor and control the operation of geothermal power facilities and maintain and repair them as needed, and install, test and maintain residential and commercial ground-source heat pumps. Core tasks include monitoring and adjusting the operation of geothermal plant equipment or systems (importance 83), writing and maintaining work logs and reports (83), identifying and correcting equipment, electrical, instrument or control faults (81), collecting and recording plant or wellfield operating data (81), and performing pre- and post-installation pressure, flow and related tests on geothermal loop piping (69), plus supplementary tasks such as adjusting the generating system to meet load and distribution needs (88), maintaining electrical switchgear and process control, transmitters and instruments (79), calculating residential heat loss and heat gain (79), maintaining and calibrating or repairing instruments and control and electronic devices (79), welding high-density polyethylene piping (66), and installing and maintaining or repairing ground-source or water-source coupled heat pumps (66). Common job titles include Geothermal Service Technician, I and C Technician, Operations and Maintenance Technician, Plant Mechanic and Plant Technician; on the 49-9099.01 page O*NET shows that the occupation's main industries in the US include administrative and support services and manufacturing (the industry data on that page come from the parent occupation 49-9099.00). subject.summary: Geothermal Technicians corresponds to the exact occupation O*NET/SOC 49-9099.01 'Geothermal Technicians': perform technical activities at power plants or individual installations necessary for the generation of power from geothermal energy sources, monitor and control operating activities at geothermal power generation facilities and perform maintenance and repairs as necessary, and install, test, and maintain residential and commercial geothermal heat pumps; common job titles include Geothermal Service Technician, I and C Technician, Operations and Maintenance Technician, Plant Mechanic, and Plant Technician. Official scope text: Perform technical activities at power plants or individual installations necessary for the generation of power from geothermal energy sources. Monitor and control operating activities at geothermal power generation facilities and perform maintenance and repairs as necessary. Install, test, and maintain residential and commercial geothermal heat pumps. Measure note: the U.S. wages, employment, and industry data presented by O*NET on the 49-9099.01 page are taken from the parent occupation 49-9099.00 (Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers, All Other); this page labels them truthfully as parent-occupation measures and does not call them values for this exact occupation itself.
